_headline: ANSWERED: visual is a LEARNED SHORTCUT, not non-predictive. The SERVED checkpoint already predicts the brain from visual streams ALONE at r=0.0752 (58% of its full-stream accuracy) — nobody had measured this. 400 steps (1.8 minutes of H100) of forcing visual-only prediction raised that to r=0.1001 (76% of full), a +33% relative gain, without harming audio or overall accuracy.
_output_note: NEW checkpoint. The served checkpoint was not modified.
data: real fMRI — 214 video train entries, 112 video val windows. NOT simulated.
verdict: SHORTCUT, not non-predictive. This is the discriminating result the four diagnostic scripts were built to get, and it comes down clearly on the shortcut side.

The strongest single number is PRE-finetune, i.e. true of the SERVED model today: visual_only = 0.0752, which is 58% of what the model achieves with all six streams. The visual encoders are not inert. They were never inert. They predict the brain from pixels alone.

Forcing is trivially easy: 400 steps and 1.8 minutes of H100 lifted visual_only 33% relative (0.0752 -> 0.1001, 76% of full accuracy). A pathway that improves that fast on that little compute was under-trained, not incapable.
It did no harm: audio_only was unchanged (0.1270 -> 0.1271) and base_all did not drop (0.1297 -> 0.1312). The audio pathway was not traded away.

the_subtlety_that_matters._finding: Visual is INDIVIDUALLY PREDICTIVE but MARGINALLY REDUNDANT, and these are not in conflict.
the_subtlety_that_matters.shuffling_visual_costs: 10.4% of base (permutation null, ci95 excludes zero)
the_subtlety_that_matters.why_they_differ: Shuffled visual injects ACTIVELY WRONG content; absent visual merely withholds. Wrong visual hurts ~5x more than missing visual. So the model genuinely reads the visual stream — mismatched pixels degrade it — but in a naturalistic movie corpus what you see is largely predictable from what you hear and what is said, so visual's UNIQUE contribution over audio+text is small (~2%).
the_subtlety_that_matters.implication: 'Mary cannot see' is false. 'Visual adds little on top of audio+text IN THIS CORPUS' is true. The ceiling here is the corpus's audio/visual redundancy, not the encoder.

limitations: One run, one seed, 400 steps, 1.8 minutes. This is a hypothesis test, explicitly, not a trained model. mary_visual_force_v1 is NOT a ship candidate.
No confidence intervals on any of these eval numbers. base_all 0.1297 -> 0.1312 is well within plausible noise and should NOT be reported as an improvement.

delta_swap_visual here uses the WEAK roll-by-half permutation (it reproduces -0.0059 exactly), so the -0.0059 -> -0.0079 shift understates the effect and is not the number to quote. Use the permutation null (-0.0135) from visual_swap_null_2026-07-16.json.

Forcing did NOT make the FULL model lean on visual much more (swap delta -0.0059 -> -0.0079). The shortcut persists when audio is available. Visual-only capability improved; full-model reliance barely moved.
112 val windows. Absolute accuracy remains low (r~0.13 on responsive vertices).
what_this_changes: The program has operated on 'the served model ignores visual content (swap-test delta ~0.3%)' — that premise, written in finetune_visual_force.py's own docstring, is now falsified from three directions: the 0.3% was slowfast measured alone; the permutation was weak; and visual-only prediction was never measured at all and turns out to be 58% of full accuracy. Production still runs ACTIVE_STREAMS = ('beats','whisper','qwen_ctx') (qualia/core/mary_engine.py:21), i.e. with a demonstrably predictive visual pathway switched off. Whether to turn it on is now a cost/benefit question (slowfast needs A100-40GB, qwen_vl A100-80GB per asset) against a ~2% marginal accuracy gain — NOT the 'it does nothing anyway' question it has been treated as.
